title: Halicin: a deep-learning-identified antibiotic validated in vitro and in mice, with no verified human outcome
summary: A deep-learning screen identified halicin, active in vitro and in mice and confirmed by other labs; no human outcome (general benefit without an event).
account: A Cell paper published on 20 February 2020 by Jonathan Stokes, Regina Barzilay, James Collins and colleagues at MIT, the Broad Institute, Harvard and McMaster University reported halicin, a molecule identified by a directed-message-passing neural network trained on 2,335 molecules to predict inhibition of E. coli growth. Halicin, originally investigated as a kinase inhibitor for diabetes, is structurally divergent from conventional antibiotics; it reduced Acinetobacter baumannii in a mouse wound model and cleared Clostridioides difficile in a mouse infection model. Independent laboratories at KACST in Riyadh (December 2021) and Central South University in Changsha (September 2022) confirmed antibacterial activity in vitro, the latter also in a mouse abscess model. No clinical use or human trial result appears in any source on file.
purpose: Built to predict molecules that inhibit bacterial growth and surface antibiotic candidates; halicin was that purpose.
system: Directed-message-passing neural network (D-MPNN) for antibacterial activity prediction (Chemprop-style, MIT)
developer: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (Collins and Barzilay laboratories) with the Broad Institute
deployer: MIT / Broad Institute / McMaster University research teams

ratings.reason: General benefit without an event: the sources document in vitro and murine results and independent laboratory confirmation, but no individually attributable real-world outcome such as a treated patient or an approved drug.

ai_role.statement: The neural network's prediction selected halicin for testing from compounds not previously recognized as antibiotics; wet-lab experiments by the authors and later by independent groups confirmed the activity. The outcome so far is a laboratory and animal-model result.

evidence.citation: Stokes, J. M. et al. (2020). A Deep Learning Approach to Antibiotic Discovery. Cell 180, 688–702 (PMC8349178).
evidence.title: A deep learning approach to antibiotic discovery
evidence.quote: sterilization of 3 out of 4 mice after 72 hr of treatment, and 4 out of 4 mice after 96 hr of treatment.

evidence.citation: Booq, R. Y., Tawfik, E. A., Alfassam, H. A., Alfahad, A. J. and Alyamani, E. J. (2021). Assessment of the Antibacterial Efficacy of Halicin against Pathogenic Bacteria. Antibiotics 10(12), 1480 (PMC8698312).
evidence.title: Assessment of the Antibacterial Efficacy of Halicin against Pathogenic Bacteria
evidence.quote: The new antibacterial agent was able to inhibit all tested gram-positive and gram-negative bacterial strains, but in different concentrations—including the A. baumannii multidrug-resistant (MDR) isolate.

evidence.citation: Hussain, Z. et al. (2022). Study on antibacterial effect of halicin (SU3327) against Enterococcus faecalis and Enterococcus faecium. Pathogens and Disease 80(1), ftac037.
evidence.title: Study on antibacterial effect of halicin (SU3327) against Enterococcus faecalis and Enterococcus faecium
evidence.quote: the minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) of halicin against different strains of Enterococcus faecalis and Enterococcus faecium ranged from 4 to 8 μg/ml.

produced_by: A growth-inhibition training set of a few thousand molecules
A message-passing network ranking large chemical libraries
Wet-lab confirmation of predicted actives and animal-model testing
must_hold: Predicted compounds must be available for synthesis or purchase
Activity must be confirmed experimentally; a verified real-world outcome would require clinical use

echoes.setting: Abaucin, a narrow-spectrum anti-Acinetobacter baumannii compound identified by a neural network trained on about 7,500 screened molecules (McMaster and MIT), controlled infection in a mouse wound model; preclinical only

headline: MIT neural network finds halicin, active in vitro and in mice

later.note: An independent laboratory at KACST in Riyadh confirmed halicin's in vitro activity against gram-positive and gram-negative strains, including a multidrug-resistant A. baumannii isolate; the compound remains preclinical.
later.quote: The new antibacterial agent was able to inhibit all tested gram-positive and gram-negative bacterial strains, but in different concentrations—including the A. baumannii multidrug-resistant (MDR) isolate.

claim_basis: Two independent peer-reviewed studies and the makers' peer-reviewed study are on file. There is no finding by a regulator or court.
